EXPORT_PACK_AR_TOOLTIP:
Set by the chosen file type (.ar).
The exported files (city, geometry, bound, texture, tune, race and jpg folders) and the geometry and texture folders of the city are packed into the chosen .ar file (a zip archive), named after the exported city file name of the city properties (or the archive name, when it is empty), to put in the game folder. No loose files are written.
The hudmap preview is saved next to the archive.
EXPORT_CPVS_TOOLTIP:
The visible rooms of each room (city/<city>.cpvs): the game draws only the rooms seen from the room of the camera, with their objects.
Computed from the facade bounds, roofs and ground of the city; a few seconds to a minute in large cities.
EXPORT_CPVS_ACCURATE_TOOLTIP: Computes the CPVS with more viewpoints in each room, more eye heights and a finer grid: fewer rooms appearing late, but it takes much longer (minutes in large cities).
BAI_RD_DIVIDER_TOOLTIP: A divided BAI road, as a PSDL road with a divider: the divider width is the space between its two directions
RD_GENERATE_LOW_LOD_TEX_TOOLTIP: Make the low LOD texture of this double road from its textures and widths when the city is exported, in the texture folder of the export, instead of using the low LOD texture above. It follows every change of the road.
RD_LOWER_WO_SW: Lower if w/o sidewalks (can look weird ingame)
RD_FREEWAY_TOOLTIP: Ambient vehicles go faster on this road (BAI freeway flag)
RD_CABLE_CAR_TOOLTIP: Cable car rails in both directions (as on the San Francisco cable car roads); connect the roads of a line through intersections
RD_CABLE_CAR_OFFSET_TOOLTIP: Distance of each cable car rail from the center of the road (0: 2.5 m, as in San Francisco)
TP_FORCE_BOTTOM_TOOLTIP: Draw a bottom wall 1 m under the patch, e.g. under a patch between two elevated roads. The game doesn't draw it under terrain patches: it is exported as a PKG mesh
RD_RL_FORCE_BOTTOM_TOOLTIP: Draw the bottom wall (with the ground texture of the Railing tab) under the road also without walls on both sides. The game draws it only with walls on both sides: otherwise it is exported as a PKG mesh
TP_DELETE_BORDER_MESH_WARNING: Are you sure you want to remove the selected railing?
CP_TRAIN_LINES_TOOLTIP: Underground trains (as in London): each line is a train going back and forth between its first and last point
TRAIN_LINE_POINTS_TOOLTIP: The path of the train, from one station to the other (the train stops at the first and the last point)
CP_DECALS_TOOLTIP: Textured strips on the roads and the ground (e.g. zebra zigzags, yellow boxes, rails), exported to decals.pathset with the PATHSET
DECAL_TEXTURE_TOOLTIP: The texture of the decal (it must be in the game, e.g. decal_zigzag_l, decal_x_inter_l, r4i_rails_f), tiled along it in square tiles as wide as the decal; its transparent parts show the road
DECAL_WIDTH_TOOLTIP: The width of the decal in metres (the side of the texture tiles)
DECAL_POINTS_TOOLTIP: The centre line of the decal, on the roads or the ground (each piece of it is drawn by the game with the room of its start)
CP_CABLE_CAR_RAIL_DECALS_TOOLTIP: Decals along the rails of the cable car roads, going on through the intersections from a road of a line into the next one (as in San Francisco)
CP_CABLE_CAR_RAIL_TEXTURE_TOOLTIP: The texture of the decals of the cable car rails (r4i_rails_f if not set)
CP_CABLE_CAR_RAIL_WIDTH_TOOLTIP: The width of the decals of the cable car rails in metres (2 if not set)
ASSUME_MM2HOOK_TOOLTIP: Turn this on if the city is meant to be played with MM2Hook (with the default settings of the hook), instead of stock MM2. It lets you edit the roll of the road points, adds the third model to the example parked cars and adapts the export warnings about the texture references. It doesn't change how the rest of the city is exported.
CP_SKY_MESH_TOOLTIP: The sky dome model, written in the .sky file of the city (sky_dome, as in San Francisco, if not set; London uses sky_dome_l). The game shows a black sky without it.
CP_SKY_HEIGHT_TOOLTIP: Height of the sky dome added to its height from the camera, in metres (0 if not set)
CP_SKY_CAMERA_HEIGHT_FACTOR_TOOLTIP: How much the sky dome follows the height of the camera: 1 keeps it at the same height from the camera, 0 leaves it fixed (0.95 if not set, as in the stock cities)
CP_SKY_ROTATION_SPEED_TOOLTIP: How fast the sky dome turns around, in radians per second (0.005 if not set, as in the stock cities)
RD_TRAFFIC_LIGHT_OPPOSITE_ROAD: Place traffic lights on the opposite road
RD_TRAFFIC_LIGHT_OPPOSITE_ROAD_INV_START: Swap start light side on opposite road
RD_TRAFFIC_LIGHT_OPPOSITE_ROAD_INV_END: Swap end light side on opposite road
BLOCK_NUMBER_TOOLTIP:
Used only for MM2, if not empty and greater than 0 it will override the automatic assignment.
Be careful when using it in conjunction with railings, as it could lead to unexpected results.
RD_SW_UV_TOOLTIP:
Fixes the UV coordinates of the sidewalks vertical border face.
Not supported in MM2
RD_ECHO_TOOLTIP: For galleries and underground roads, adds an echo to the sound when on it
UV_MULT_TOOLTIP:
Multiplies the U/V texure coordinate by this amount
Not supported in MM2
RD_RD_HEIGHT_TOOLTIP: Always 0.15 in MM2. If set to a value different than 0.15, the sidewalk will be slanted in MM2
TP_MERGE_TOOLTIP:
If checked, when exporting for MM2, this patch will be assigned to the same block of other connected patches which have this flag set too (note: connected means: at least one edge in common)
Note: be careful if you add railings, as they can only be placed on the block perimeter
PROP_ELEM_RND_TOOLTIP:
If unchecked, meshes are chosen sequentially, if checked, randomly.
Even if checked the result won't be exactly the same as in MM2, since there props are placed according to an apparently random pattern (which is always the same though)
UV_MULT_SW_TOOLTIP: Multiplies the U coordinate for road-style sidewalks by this amount. Not supported in MM2 (equivalent is 1)
RD_FIX_SIDEWALKS_UV_TOOLTIP: Uses road-style UV coordinates for the sidewalks. Use sparingly, as it may look bad (or even break in MM2) when the sidewalk does not have 4 distinct sides (e.g. when going from a road with sidewalks to another without them)
RD_COPLANAR_TOOLTIP:
In Midtown Madness 2 the road colliders are quads, this means that the 4 corner vertices must be coplanar to make the mesh the same as the collider.
Roads that bend only on one axis (Y (left-right) or Z (up-down)) are not a problem.
The problem arises when a road bends on both the Y and Z axes (e.g. a curved slope).
This option tries to make the segments of such roads coplanar by rearranging the vertices.
This does not always work, if the curve is not slight the result will be horrible.
FIX_BOUND_TOOLTIP:
If checked, it will duplicate the facade bound and assign it to the room in front of it in addition to the room behind it.
This can help make the bound work consistently. (in case it doesn't always work)
Use sparingly.
On building lines it is only used if 'front only' is checked
EXPORT_PKGS_TOOLTIP:
Writes the elements with "Export to PKG" set as PKG files (in the geometry folder) and bound files (in the bound folder).
Their INST entries and empty PSDL room are written anyway.
EXPORT_PSDL_CAP_MATERIALS_TOOLTIP:
Stock MM2 and tools like MM2 City Toolkit cannot handle PSDL files with more than 511 textures, enabling this flag will cap texture IDs to 511 if greater.
It will break them though if this happens, use it only for testing.
If disabled, there is still a cap of 2047 materials.
RD_LOWER_WO_SW_TOOLTIP: It will look weird if the road is connected to an intersection where other roads have sidewalks, as they will always be 15cm high ingame
RD_WARP_TOOLTIP: For PSDL rooms that lay atop another, e.g. when there's a bridge going over something
RD_TRAFFIC_LIGHT_OPPOSITE_ROAD_TOOLTIP: Places each traffic light on the opposite road (i.e. U.S. style)
RD_TRAFFIC_LIGHT_OPPOSITE_ROAD_ADJ_TOOLT: Shifts the traffic light by N roads (clockwise)
RD_TRAFFIC_LIGHT_SWAP_TOOLTIP: For use in cities with left-hand traffic
RD_TRAFFIC_LIGHT_OPPOSITE_ROAD_IN_OFFSET: Only used when the traffic light is on the opposite road
TRAFFIC_CAR_FREQUENCY_TOOLTIP: e.g. 20 for car A, 60 for car B (unset is considered as 1), it will become 25% for car A and 75% for car B
PROFESSIONAL_TOOLTIP: If left empty the amateur value(s) will be used for both difficulties
DO_NOT_EXPORT_TOOLTIP: If checked, this object will not be exported
TRANSF_P_ROLL_TOOLTIP: Banking of the road sections at this point, in degrees (positive raises the right side). To edit it, turn on Assume using MM2Hook in the city properties.
EXPORT_HUDMAP_TOOLTIP:
Draws the map of the city: the map of the HUD in the game (texture/<city>_hudmap*.tex, geometry/hudmap_<city>.pkg, tune/<city>.mmHudMap) and the maps of the race menus, with the map labels (jpg/<city>_maproam.jpg and jpg/<city>_map<race>.jpg).
Previews are saved as <city>_hudmap_preview.png (without labels) and <city>_hudmap_labels_preview.png (with the roam labels). Needs the Python module Pillow.
CP_MAP_LABELS_TOOLTIP: District names, parks, etc. on the menu maps. The Hudmap section shows the core-generated label previews; export also writes <city>_hudmap_labels_preview.png with the roam labels.
CP_HUDMAP_METERS_PER_PIXEL_TOOLTIP: The scale of the map of the HUD (5.5 if not set, as in the stock cities): keep the map within 16 tiles
CP_HUDMAP_TILE_SIZE_TOOLTIP: The size of the textures of the map of the HUD (the stock cities use 256)
CP_HUDMAP_MARGIN_TOOLTIP: The space around the city in the map of the HUD, in metres (100 if not set)
CP_HUDMAP_OUTLINE_WIDTH_TOOLTIP: The width of the outline of the roads in the in-game hudmap, in pixels, drawn only against the ground and the buildings (1 if not set, as San Francisco; 0 for none, as London). The race maps of the menus have no outline, as the stock ones
CP_HUDMAP_COLOR_TOOLTIP: A color as #RRGGBB (the default if not set)
CP_HUDMAP_COLOR_BACKGROUND_TOOLTIP: A color as #RRGGBB for uncovered areas of the HUD and menu maps, and around the map of the HUD. Uses the Water color if not set.
CP_HUDMAP_COLOR_WATER_TOOLTIP: A color as #RRGGBB for water surfaces (the default if not set). Also used as the background when Background is empty.
CP_HUDMAP_HIDE_ARROWS_TOOLTIP: Leave out the arrows that show the direction of the one-way roads on the maps
CP_HUDMAP_LABEL_FONT_TOOLTIP: A .ttf or .otf font for exported labels (absolute, or relative to Files/common/MidtownMadness2). Uses the bundled stock-style Liberation Sans Bold if empty. The editor preview uses the bundled font outlines.
MAP_LABEL_TEXT_TOOLTIP: The text of the label (shown in upper case)
MAP_LABEL_SIZE_TOOLTIP: Text size in pixels of the race maps (242x184 images), 6.75 if not set. Roam-map names use 75% of this size.
MAP_LABEL_ANGLE_TOOLTIP: The rotation of the text in degrees (counterclockwise)
HUDMAP_CATEGORY_TOOLTIP:
How the element is drawn on the maps of the HUD and of the race menus.
Auto: terrain patches by their texture (grass and water by the physics materials of city/materials.csv, or by name), ground otherwise; roads and intersections by their texture too, road otherwise; buildings as buildings; movable bridges as roads; mesh instances are not drawn
CONVERSION_ERROR_MISSING: The element to convert was not found
PROP_PARKED_DISTANCE_TOOLTIP: Distance between the parking slots, in metres (from 5.25 to 100). The game decides which slots are used and which cars they get: the preview is only an example.
PROP_PARKED_REVERSE_TOOLTIP: Turn the cars of this row around. By default the cars of a road row follow the traffic of the nearest lanes; on a prop line they run against the direction of the spline.
INST_LANDMARK_TOOLTIP: Visible from every angle, for monuments and other whole objects. Uncheck it for facades, which are visible from the front only
INST_SIMPLE_COLLISION_TOOLTIP: Wheels don't collide with this mesh. Only works together with Landmark
INST_BANGER_TOOLTIP: Creates a banger instead of a static mesh. Don't combine it with Landmark or No wheel collision
INST_MULTIROOM_TOOLTIP: Places the mesh in all the rooms its bound touches, as the tunnels of the original cities. The mesh needs a bound file. Only works with Landmark unchecked
INST_PAINT_JOB_TOOLTIP: Which paint job of the mesh to use, from 0 to 255. Facades of the original cities use it to vary their look
RAIL_ROOM_TOOLTIP: The road, intersection or terrain patch whose perimeter the rail follows (its room in the game). Set by the first point; when that point is on several of them, you choose it
GENERATE_RAIL_DECALS_TOOLTIP: Create editable tram rail connections across this intersection. Delete previous decals manually before regenerating.
CHECK_OPPONENTS_TOOLTIP: Check whether the opponents reach the finish as the game drives them: each waypoint must be on an intersection and a single road must join consecutive ones, otherwise the opponent drives straight through whatever is in the way. On a circuit, the last waypoint must be on the intersection of the first one. The routes are drawn over the city while the results are shown.
LOD_TEXTURE_ERROR_MISSING: The road and sidewalk textures of the road are needed to generate the low LOD texture, but were not found
LOD_TEXTURE_ERROR_WIDTHS: The widths of the road leave no space for the lanes or the sidewalks
BOAT_MODEL_TOOLTIP: What moves along the route. The sailboat is the default model of the sailboat path file, the others are the stock models of the game (the game must have them). The car ferry is written to the ferry path file
BOAT_SPEED_TOOLTIP: The average speed in metres per second (each boat varies by 1 m/s in game), in steps of 0.25. 0 uses the default of the model (2 for ducks, 20 for sailboards, 5 for the others). Ignored by the car ferry, which always moves at the same speed
PARKED_CAR_PREVIEW_HINT: Example car only. The game chooses the model and paint and may leave this slot empty.
CHECKPOINTS_CREATE_HINT: To add one, use Create > Checkpoint
POLICE_CARS_CREATE_HINT: Add police cars with Create > Police car while this container is selected.
OPPONENTS_CREATE_HINT: Add opponents with Create > Opponent while this race setup is selected.
PROPS_CREATE_HINT: To add one, use Create > Props
MAP_LABEL_CREATE_HINT: Add labels from Create > Map label while the Hudmap section is open.
BRIDGE_MODEL_TOOLTIP: The model of a leaf, with its length along Z. Stock: giz_bridge01_l (30 m), giz_waterloo_l (23.18 m), giz_bridge02_l (20 m). A custom model needs a short name, and uses the banger data in the tune/banger folder of the city, or gets one from its size.
BRIDGE_GENERATE_MESH_TOOLTIP: Make the model of this bridge from the roads its controls are attached to: their widths, sidewalks, divider and textures, and the distance and angle of the hinges, instead of using the model above. The editor shows it and follows every change, and the export writes it with its collision and banger data in the export folder. Both leaves use one model: if the roads differ, it fits the widest one.
BRIDGE_MESH_ERROR_NO_ROADS: Attach a control of the bridge to a road end to generate its model
BRIDGE_MESH_ERROR_WIDTHS: The widths of the road leave no space for the lanes or the sidewalks
BRIDGE_MESH_ERROR_LENGTH: The hinges are too close to generate a model
BRIDGE_MESH_ERROR_ANGLE: The road is too far from the direction of the bridge to generate a model (at most 60 degrees)
BRIDGE_TRUSS_TEXTURE_TOOLTIP: Generated model: the truss on the sides and ends, also used for its bottom. It can have transparent parts. The texture must be in the game or in the texture folder of the city.
BRIDGE_BOTTOM_TEXTURE_TOOLTIP: Generated model: the plate under the road, seen through the truss.
BRIDGE_RAIL_TEXTURE_TOOLTIP: Generated model: the railings. As in the stock tl_bridgetrim_l, the railing is in the middle band of the texture.
BRIDGE_PAIRED_TOOLTIP: Two leaves facing each other. Off: one leaf at the first hinge; the other point sets its direction. Models keep their original size.
BRIDGE_BEHAVIOR_TOOLTIP: Native MM2 movement: 27 degrees, about 9.4 seconds to move, with 10-second waits. Proximity reacts to the player and opponents within 100 m.
BRIDGE_PREVIEW_TOOLTIP: Editor only. Previewing another pose does not change the exported bridge or its behavior.
BRIDGE_REPLACES_TOOLTIP: For a race-owned bridge, pick the city bridge to replace in that race: it is hidden while the race is selected. Leave empty to add another bridge. The other city bridges remain in that race.
OPPONENT_WAYPOINTS_HINT: Put a waypoint on every intersection the opponent drives through: the game needs them there, so the waypoints go only on the centers of the intersections. The last point is the finish and goes anywhere: to add waypoints after the last one, select the finish and use the click mode "Add before selected". On a circuit, put the first waypoint on the intersection behind the start and end the loop on that intersection again, with a last waypoint before the finish (click the first waypoint).
BRIDGE_PLACEMENT_HINT: Click the first hinge, then the opposite one: a cyan free road end attaches the hinge to it. Click mode > Place the points one by one places them again. Models keep their original size. Leave the moving deck clear of static roads. Import MM2 game assets for the stock models.
BRIDGES_CREATE_HINT: To add one, use Create > Moving objects > Movable bridge
